questions.title: Type family
questions.context: Menus today mix a tall narrow font for headings with a normal font for small words, and a few places use only the narrow one. From the couch narrow letters get harder to read, but big narrow numbers look strong. The same sample screen is drawn in four font setups so you can compare them.
questions.question: Which font setup should every menu and the on-screen display use?

options.label: Narrow for everything
options.description: Every word in the tall narrow face. Most words per line, strongest numbers, how much of the game looks today.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382 and scaled to 1920x1080 (a clean top-down street with no on-screen display), darkened to 35 percent brightness. Palette: panel #14171a, line #2e3337, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e with ink #0d1200. Centred card 1200x720 at x360 y180: fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius, padding 40px. Inside: title 'Settings' 56px; tab strip under it 'The raid', 'Audio', 'Controls', 'Display' at 28px with the first tab active (4px lime underline); four rows 64px high with 1px #2e3337 dividers ('Damage' 'Standard', 'Raid length' 'Standard', 'Master volume' 'Full', 'Shared sight' 'On'; name left, value right, both 28px); a lime button 'Resume' 280x72 (28px text, ink #0d1200) bottom-left; bottom-right a sample ammo '12 / 24' at 120px with 'Scav pistol' 26px muted under it. FONT FOR THIS OPTION: Barlow Condensed everywhere: weight 800 for the title and numbers, 700 for tabs and buttons, 600 for rows and values; letter-spacing +0.02em; sentence case only.

options.label: Narrow headings, normal-width body
options.description: Big words and numbers stay narrow and punchy; small words get wider letters that read better from far away.
options.spec: Same backdrop, card, rows, button and ammo sample as option A (see A for sizes and palette). FONT FOR THIS OPTION: Barlow Condensed 800 for the title, tabs, buttons and the ammo number; Barlow (normal width) 500 for the row names and row values; letter-spacing +0.01em on the Barlow text; everything sentence case.

options.label: Normal width everywhere
options.description: One calm, wide family. Looks cleaner and more modern, but fewer words fit per line and numbers are less punchy.
options.spec: Same backdrop, card, rows, button and ammo sample as option A. FONT FOR THIS OPTION: Barlow (normal width) only: weight 600 for the title, tabs, buttons and the ammo number (600 is the heaviest Barlow weight embedded today; going heavier means embedding one more file, about 40 KB), weight 500 for rows and values; tabular figures for numbers; letter-spacing 0; sentence case.

options.label: Round and friendly
options.description: A rounder face with soft corners. Warmer and a bit more playful, closest to Fortnite, but less 'shooter'.
options.spec: Same backdrop, card, rows, button and ammo sample as option A, but the lime button gets an 8px radius and the card 8px. FONT FOR THIS OPTION: Rubik (already embedded, variable weight): 700 for the title and ammo number, 600 for tabs and buttons, 500 for rows and values; letter-spacing 0; sentence case.

questions.pick_reason: Big words and numbers stay punchy while small words get wider letters for the TV, and both fonts are already built into the game so it works offline.

questions.title: Text sizes for the TV
questions.context: At the party the screens are 6 to 10 feet away, and the demo already makes the on-screen display 50 percent bigger. The base sizes still decide how big the smallest text and the one big number really are. Each option shows the same screen with its real pixel sizes and how tall the small letters are on a 55 inch TV.
questions.question: How big should the smallest text, normal text, titles and the one big number be?

options.label: Compact
options.description: Smallest text 16, normal 20, titles 32, big number 56. Fits a lot on screen; from 8 feet the small text is fine print.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382 scaled to 1920x1080 (clean street), darkened to 40 percent. Palette: panel #14171a, line #2e3337, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e. Fonts: Barlow Condensed 700 (title, numbers), Barlow 500 (rows). Card 1300x780 centred (fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius, padding 40px). Draw: title 'Paused' at the TITLE size; three rows 'Resume', 'Settings', 'Feedback' at the BODY size with values 'On', 'Full', 'Off' right-aligned at the SMALL size; a hint bar along the card bottom with key caps 'A Select' and 'B Back' at the SMALL size; a stat 'Armour 60' at the SMALL size; the big number '12 / 24' at the HERO size in lime. Along the very bottom of the screen a ribbon (#0b0c0d, 28px text) says: 'Small 16, body 20, title 32, hero 56. Small letters on a 55 inch TV at 8 ft: 0.7 cm tall, 1.1 cm in the demo (x1.5).' SIZES FOR THIS OPTION: small 16, body 20, title 32, hero 56.

options.label: Roomy
options.description: Smallest text 20, normal 26, titles 40, big number 72. In the demo's 1.5x the small text becomes 30, comfortable from 8 feet.
options.spec: Same backdrop, card (grow it to 1500x860 to fit), content and palette as option A. SIZES FOR THIS OPTION: small 20, body 26, title 40, hero 72. Ribbon text: 'Small 20, body 26, title 40, hero 72. Small letters on a 55 inch TV at 8 ft: 0.9 cm tall, 1.3 cm in the demo (x1.5).'

options.label: Couch first
options.description: Smallest text 24, normal 32, titles 48, big number 96. Easiest on a TV, but menus get big and fewer rows fit.
options.spec: Same backdrop, content and palette as option A; the card is 1700x960 at x110 y60 so the bigger text fits (rows may need two columns of values). SIZES FOR THIS OPTION: small 24, body 32, title 48, hero 96. Ribbon text: 'Small 24, body 32, title 48, hero 96. Small letters on a 55 inch TV at 8 ft: 1.1 cm tall, 1.6 cm in the demo (x1.5).'

questions.pick_reason: With the demo's 1.5x the small text lands at 30 px (about 1.3 cm letters), which reads from 8 feet, and A is still under the comfortable mark even in the demo.

questions.title: The exact lime
questions.context: You picked a lime yellow accent for the selected item and the main button. Lime runs from almost lemon yellow to almost green, and it looks different over the orange floors and green grass in a raid. Each option shows the same pieces so you can judge which one jumps out most.
questions.question: Which exact lime yellow should be the accent?

options.label: Lemon lime #f6f02c
options.description: The yellowest of the four, close to Fortnite's Ready button. Also the closest cousin to the old amber.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382, scaled to 1920x1080, full brightness. Palette: panel #14171a, line #2e3337, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e. ACCENT FOR THIS OPTION: #f6f02c with ink #0d1200 on it. Draw: (1) ammo plate 460x200 at x1364 y820 (fill rgba(20,23,26,.9), 1px #2e3337, 4px radius) with 'Scav pistol' 26px muted and '12 / 24' 110px in the accent; (2) tab strip at x96 y70 with tabs 'Guns', 'Heals', 'Parts' at 28px, 'Guns' active in white with a 4px accent underline; (3) button 'Resume' 300x72 at x96 y160, accent fill, ink text 28px; (4) a belt of 5 slots 96x96 at x560 y930 (fill #14171a) with the third slot ringed 4px in the accent; (5) a selected list row 520x64 at x96 y280: 6px accent bar on the left, fill 14 percent accent, text 'Grenade' 28px; (6) a visibility strip at x96 y980: the text 'Goal +400 SP' 36px in the accent on three plates 260x56 in a row: dark #14171a, floor orange #c9774a, grass green #4b6a3a; (7) a chip at the bottom-right with the hex and name of the shade in 28px white on #0b0c0d.

options.label: Volt #e4ff2e
options.description: Bright electric yellow-green. The brightest of the four, so it pops on dark, orange and green grounds.
options.spec: Same layout, backdrop and pieces as option A. ACCENT FOR THIS OPTION: #e4ff2e with ink #0d1200 on it. Chip text: 'Volt #e4ff2e'.

options.label: Lime #c4f12e
options.description: A clearly green-leaning lime. Fresh and modern, a little less bright, and closer to the grass colour.
options.spec: Same layout, backdrop and pieces as option A. ACCENT FOR THIS OPTION: #c4f12e with ink #0d1200 on it. Chip text: 'Lime #c4f12e'.

options.label: Green lime #a8e82a
options.description: The greenest and softest. Easiest on the eyes, but the least 'yellow' and the weakest against grass.
options.spec: Same layout, backdrop and pieces as option A. ACCENT FOR THIS OPTION: #a8e82a with ink #0d1200 on it. Chip text: 'Green lime #a8e82a'.

questions.pick_reason: Highest brightness of the four (about 17:1 against the dark) so it stays visible over orange floors and grass, yet it is clearly not the old amber.

questions.title: Card and panel look
questions.context: You want windows to be a centred card with an X in the corner that fills nearly the whole screen. How that card is built (sharp or round, flat or glassy, border or glow, where the X sits) sets the feel of every menu. Same Settings window in four builds.
questions.question: How should the big window cards look?

options.label: Solid slab
options.description: Flat dark card, thin border, slightly rounded, no glow. Cleanest and always readable.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382, scaled to 1920x1080, darkened to 50 percent. Palette: void #0b0c0d, panel #14171a, raised #1e2225, line #2e3337, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e with ink #0d1200. Card 1728x972 at x96 y54 (90 percent of the screen). Content: header with 'Settings' 48px at left padding 40px and a close X at the top-right; four rows 72px high ('Damage' 'Standard', 'Raid length' 'Standard', 'Master volume' 'Full', 'Shared sight' 'On', 28px, the first row focused with a 6px lime bar and 14 percent lime wash); footer with a ghost button 'Back' 200x64 and a lime button 'Done' 200x64. BUILD FOR THIS OPTION: fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337 border, radius 4px, no shadow, no gradient; a 3px lime tab 48px wide on the top-left edge; the close X is a 48x48 square ghost button (1px #4a5257 border, 2px white X glyph) inside the header at the top-right; rows separated by 1px #2e3337 lines.

options.label: Frosted glass
options.description: See-through blurred card with a soft shadow and round corners. Modern and airy, a bit lower contrast.
options.spec: Same backdrop, content and layout as option A. BUILD FOR THIS OPTION: fill rgba(16,19,22,.62) with backdrop blur 22px; 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.12); radius 16px; shadow 0 30px 80px rgba(0,0,0,.55); a 1px inner top highlight rgba(255,255,255,.06); the close X is a 56px circle (fill rgba(255,255,255,.10)) inside the header at the top-right; rows have no dividers, the focused row is a rounded 12px lime-wash pill.

options.label: Cut corners
options.description: Sharp card with two diagonal cut corners and a thin lime edge line. Feels like a Halo 4 menu.
options.spec: Same backdrop, content and layout as option A. BUILD FOR THIS OPTION: fill #101418, 1px border #3a4a55, radius 0 but two 28px diagonal cuts at the top-right and bottom-left corners; a 3px lime line 160px long along the top-left edge; a faint inner glow 1px rgba(228,255,46,.10); the close X is a 48px square with its own diagonal cut sitting in the top-right cut corner; rows have 1px dividers.

options.label: Big soft card, hanging X
options.description: Very round, soft shadow with a faint lime halo, pill-shaped rows and a round X that hangs off the corner.
options.spec: Same backdrop, content and layout as option A. BUILD FOR THIS OPTION: fill #181c20, no border, radius 28px, shadow 0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.6) plus a faint lime halo 0 0 60px rgba(228,255,46,.08); rows are 56px high pills (radius 18px, fill #1e2225, focused row lime-washed); the close X is a 64px round button (fill #232830, white 2px X) whose centre sits exactly on the card's top-right corner so half of it hangs outside.

questions.pick_reason: A solid slab is the easiest to read from a TV, costs the least to draw at 4K, and the blurred world behind it (next questions) already gives the modern feel.

questions.title: Selected button look
questions.context: Every button and list row needs a clear 'this one is selected' look that is identical for mouse hover and for a pad, and visible across a room. Same pause menu drawn with four ways of showing the selected button.
questions.question: How should the selected button look?

options.label: Lime fill
options.description: The selected button turns solid lime with dark text. The lime moves with you, like Fortnite's lobby.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all/25-raid-pause-box-1080.jpg with a black overlay at 55 percent and a 12px blur. Palette: panel #14171a, line #4a5257, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, danger #ff5a3c, lime #e4ff2e with ink #0d1200. Column of five buttons 520x72, gap 16, starting at x700 y250: 'Resume', 'Settings', 'Feedback', 'What's new', 'End run' (28px text). 'End run' is a danger ghost (2px #ff5a3c border, #ff5a3c text) with 32px extra space above it. At the right (x1300 y250) a state strip shows one button 360x64 in four stacked states: idle, focused, pressed (1px lower, scale .98), disabled (40 percent opacity, text 'Need 29,100 more'). A hint strip at the bottom 'A Select   B Back'. Focus sits on 'Settings'. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: focused = solid lime fill, ink text weight 700; idle = transparent with a 2px #4a5257 border and white text; on opening, focus starts on 'Resume' so the one lime button is also the main action; pressed fill #c9dd24.

options.label: Floating ring
options.description: The selected button keeps its dark fill but gets a bright lime ring a little away from it.
options.spec: Same backdrop, buttons, state strip and hint strip as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: focused = a 3px lime outline drawn 6px outside the button (radius 14px), text white, fill unchanged #14171a; the main action 'Resume' keeps a permanent lime fill with ink text (so the ring wraps it when it is focused); idle buttons have a 1px #2e3337 border.

options.label: Bar and wash
options.description: A thick lime bar on the left edge and a light lime tint behind the row. Calm, very readable in long lists.
options.spec: Same backdrop, buttons, state strip and hint strip as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: focused = a 6px lime bar on the button's left edge plus a fill of rgba(228,255,46,.14) and white text; idle buttons have no border, fill #14171a at 70 percent; the main action 'Resume' keeps a lime fill with ink text.

options.label: Lift and glow
options.description: The selected button grows a little and glows while the others dim. Lively and obvious, most 'game-like'.
options.spec: Same backdrop, buttons, state strip and hint strip as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: focused = scale 1.06, a 2px lime outline and a glow 0 0 28px rgba(228,255,46,.45); every unfocused button dims to 60 percent brightness; the main action 'Resume' keeps a lime fill with ink text.

questions.pick_reason: It is exactly your rule (lime means selected and main), it is the loudest from 10 feet, and mouse and pad can share it.

questions.title: Icons and button prompts
questions.context: Menus use small pictures (close X, backpack, heal, coin) and little button prompts like 'E Loot' or a pad's A and B. Their drawing style changes how clean or busy a screen feels. Same icon sheet in four styles.
questions.question: What style should icons and key or pad button prompts have?

options.label: Thin outline
options.description: Thin white line drawings. Light and clean; pad buttons are plain circles with a letter.
options.spec: Backdrop: #0b0c0d with notes/shots/all/23-raid-backpack-open-1080.jpg at 12 percent opacity. Sheet card 1500x820 centred (fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius). Palette: text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e. Rows: (1) 12 icons at 56px with 24px muted labels under: close X, back arrow, check, lock, backpack, map pin, gear, heal cross, grenade, bullet, coin, star; (2) key caps with a word: 'E Loot', 'Space Roll', 'R Reload', 'Tab Pause' (cap text 24px); (3) pad glyphs A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, RT each followed by a word: 'Select', 'Back', 'Reload', 'Heal', 'Previous tab', 'Next tab', 'Fire'; (4) at the bottom of the card a sample hint bar 'A Select   B Back   LB RB Tabs'. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: icons 2px white stroke, round caps, 90 percent white; key caps = 1px #4a5257 outline, 8px radius, no fill; pad glyphs = outlined circles with the letter in white; LB and RB as outlined pills.

options.label: Solid, Xbox colours
options.description: Filled icons, 3D-looking key caps and the real Xbox button colours so guests instantly know which button to press.
options.spec: Same sheet, rows and content as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: icons filled white; key caps filled #2a2f33 with a 4px darker bottom edge (3D keyboard-key look), 8px radius; pad glyphs filled circles in Xbox colours: A #6cc36c, B #e0554a, X #4aa0e0, Y #e8c93a, with a dark letter; LB, RB and RT as filled #3a4046 pills with white text.

options.label: Duotone with lime
options.description: White icons with one small lime detail each. The button you should press right now is lime.
options.spec: Same sheet, rows and content as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: icons white with exactly one detail in lime (the plus of the heal cross, the pin of the map pin, the shackle of the lock); key caps = outline with the letter in lime; pad glyphs = white filled circle with a black letter; in the sample hint bar the main prompt 'A Select' is drawn lime and the others white.

options.label: Words first
options.description: Almost no icons. Only X, arrows and checks are drawn; everything else is plain words with a simple box around keys.
options.spec: Same sheet, rows and content as option A, but rows (1) shows only close X, back arrow and check as 2px outline icons and the other nine are replaced by their words in 24px muted text. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: key caps are plain text in a 1px #4a5257 box (4px radius); pad glyphs are small mono letters in 1px circles, muted; the hint bar reads 'A Select   B Back   LB RB Tabs' with the buttons as those mono circles.

questions.pick_reason: Coloured Xbox button circles and real key caps are recognised in half a second by party guests, which helps your 'guests cannot tell how to start' worry.

questions.title: What shows behind menus
questions.context: Behind every menu or small card (pause, end of run) the game world can stay visible. Too sharp and it fights the text, too dark and the menu feels like a black wall. Same pause card over four treatments.
questions.question: How should the world look behind a menu?

options.label: Dimmed, still sharp
options.description: The world stays crisp under a dark layer. You still see what was happening.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382, scaled to 1920x1080, full brightness first. Pause card 560x680 centred at x680 y200 (fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius): title 'Paused' 48px, five rows 64px high 'Resume' (lime #e4ff2e fill, ink #0d1200), 'Settings', 'Feedback', 'What's new', 'End run' (danger #ff5a3c outline). All raid on-screen display hidden behind it. TREATMENT FOR THIS OPTION: black overlay at 70 percent, no blur.

options.label: Blurred and dimmed
options.description: The world is softly blurred and darker. Shapes and colours remain, text stands out.
options.spec: Same backdrop and pause card as option A. TREATMENT FOR THIS OPTION: blur 12px (baked once when the menu opens) plus a black overlay at 55 percent.

options.label: Nearly black
options.description: Almost black with only soft colour glows left. Very clean and the easiest to read, but the world is gone.
options.spec: Same backdrop and pause card as option A. TREATMENT FOR THIS OPTION: blur 40px plus a black overlay at 88 percent, and a vignette (radial, edges rgba(0,0,0,.6)); the world only survives as soft colour blobs.

options.label: Tinted room
options.description: Blurred and washed in a cool blue-green with a faint lime glow at the bottom, so every menu feels like the same room.
options.spec: Same backdrop and pause card as option A. TREATMENT FOR THIS OPTION: blur 16px, overlay #06141a at 62 percent, plus a faint lime glow along the bottom edge (a 220px high radial gradient rgba(228,255,46,.10) fading up).

questions.pick_reason: Your reference games blur and dim the world, it keeps the menu feeling alive, and it can be drawn once on opening so it does not cost frames at 4K.

questions.title: Pickup and kill messages
questions.context: You already decided on ten lines in the bottom-left. How those lines look decides whether they are readable on a busy map or just noise. Same seven messages in four looks.
questions.question: How should the pickup, kill and event lines look?

options.label: Plain text lines
options.description: No boxes, just bold text with a dark outline and a small coloured dot. Lightest on the eye.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped to x806 y288 w2458 h1382, scaled to 1920x1080, full brightness. Palette: text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e, gold #ffc72e, uncommon green #5fbf6a, danger #ff5a3c. Draw only the bottom-left feed from x96, newest line at the bottom (baseline y940), upwards: 'Scrap metal x3' (common grey), 'Cracked cell' (uncommon green), 'Copper wire x2' (common grey), 'Robot sentry   +120 SP' (lime), 'Golden enemy   Kill it for the hoard' (gold), 'Stronghold   2 on the map' (white), 'Contract done   Search 3 crates +200 SP' (lime). Maximum 10 lines, lines fade after 6 s, older lines at 60 percent. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: no plate; 24px Barlow 600 text with a 2px black shadow and a 1px black outline; an 8px round dot in the line colour at the left; line pitch 32px.

options.label: Slim dark plates
options.description: Each line sits on a thin dark plate with an icon and a coloured bar. Readable on any ground.
options.spec: Same backdrop and the same seven lines as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: each line on a plate 40px high (fill rgba(14,16,18,.78), radius 4px, width fits text + 24px padding), a 3px left bar in the line colour (grey info, rarity colour for loot, lime for score, danger for threats), a 24px outline icon, 22px text; line pitch 46px; new lines slide in from the left in 160 ms.

options.label: Item chips and text
options.description: Loot shows as small item tiles with a rarity bar, kills and events stay as plain text. Best to see what you picked up.
options.spec: Same backdrop and the same seven lines as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: loot lines are chips 56px high (a 56x56 item tile with a 4px rarity bar along its bottom, then the name 22px and 'x3' count on a plate rgba(14,16,18,.78)); kill, score and event lines are plain 22px text with a 2px black shadow and lime '+120 SP'; pitch 64px for chips, 32px for text.

options.label: Text feed plus score pops
options.description: A plain-text feed on the left plus big '+120 SP' pops above the belt for kills and goals, like Halo medals.
options.spec: Same backdrop and the same seven lines as option A, drawn in the plain-text style of option A. EXTRA FOR THIS OPTION: three score pops stacked above the belt at the bottom-centre (x860 y800): '+400 SP' 56px lime 800 with the small label 'Elite down' 22px white under it, '+120 SP' 44px lime at 70 percent opacity, '+200 SP' 44px lime at 40 percent opacity; each pop rises 40px and fades over 900 ms; draw a faint 1px black outline on the lime text.

questions.pick_reason: Plates keep the lines readable over bright orange floors and from a TV, and the coloured bar means a colour-blind player still reads the type of line from the icon.

questions.title: How a menu opens and closes
questions.context: Opening and closing a menu is the movement you will see most. It should feel quick and lively without making guests wait. Each option plays on a small demo card that opens, rests and closes in a loop.
questions.question: How should a menu card open and close?

options.label: Rise and fade
options.description: Fades in while rising a little. Calm and quick, no bounce.
options.spec: Demo stage 560x340 on #0b0c0d with a 480x260 card (fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius, a title bar and two rows) centred; loop: open, hold 700 ms, close, rest 400 ms. OPEN 240 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1): card opacity 0 to 1, translateY +16px to 0; scrim (black) 0 to 60 percent over the same 240 ms. Overshoot 0 percent. CLOSE 140 ms with cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1): opacity 1 to 0, translateY 0 to +8px; scrim 60 percent to 0 over 140 ms.

options.label: Pop
options.description: Grows from slightly small, a hair past full size, then settles. Lively but still quick.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and loop as option A. OPEN 280 ms: opacity 0 to 1 linearly over the first 120 ms; scale keyframes 0 percent: 0.92, 55 percent: 1.02 (ease-out cubic between), 100 percent: 1.00 (ease-in-out between), so the overshoot is 2 percent of full size; scrim 0 to 60 percent over 200 ms. CLOSE 140 ms with cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1): scale 1.00 to 0.96, opacity 1 to 0, scrim to 0 over 140 ms.

options.label: Rise from below
options.description: The card slides up from the bottom edge fast and eases in, like a drawer. No bounce.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and loop as option A. OPEN 320 ms with cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (about 95 percent of the travel in the first 120 ms): translateY +72px to 0; opacity 0 to 1 over 160 ms; scrim 0 to 60 percent over 200 ms; overshoot 0 percent. CLOSE 160 ms with cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1): translateY 0 to +40px, opacity 1 to 0 over 140 ms, scrim to 0 over 160 ms.

options.label: Zoom in from the world
options.description: The card starts a bit large and blurry and snaps into focus. Cinematic, like Halo 4.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and loop as option A. OPEN 300 ms with cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1): scale 1.08 to 1.00, blur 10px to 0, opacity 0 to 1 over 160 ms; scrim 0 to 60 percent over 300 ms; overshoot 0 percent. CLOSE 160 ms with cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1): scale 1.00 to 0.97, opacity 1 to 0, scrim to 0 over 160 ms.

questions.pick_reason: You asked for livelier motion with a little bounce; a 2 percent overshoot in 280 ms is noticeable but never makes a guest wait.

questions.title: Moving between items
questions.context: Every time you press up or down the highlight has to jump to the next item. How it travels is what makes a menu feel smooth or stiff. Each option plays a highlight moving down a five-row list and back.
questions.question: How should the highlight move from one item to the next?

options.label: Glide
options.description: One lime highlight slides to the next row and eases to a stop. Smooth, no bounce.
options.spec: Demo stage 480x360 on #0b0c0d: a list of 5 rows 56px high, 360px wide (row text 24px, fill #14171a, 1px dividers); the highlight (lime bar 4px + wash rgba(228,255,46,.14)) steps down a row every 600 ms and back up. MOTION: the highlight position follows y += (target - y) * (1 - exp(-dt / 0.04)) so it is 95 percent there in 120 ms; overshoot 0 percent; the focused row text goes from 70 percent to 100 percent white over 90 ms; the unfocused rows return to 70 percent over 90 ms.

options.label: Springy glide
options.description: The highlight slides and overshoots by a hair before settling. Smooth and a bit alive.
options.spec: Same demo stage, list and stepping as option A. MOTION: an under-damped spring with omega 30 rad/s and damping ratio 0.70: x(t) = 1 - e^(-21 t) * (cos(21.4 t) + 0.98 * sin(21.4 t)); overshoot 4.6 percent of the step (about 2.6 px on a 56px step); within 5 percent of the target at about 190 ms; the focused row text brightens 70 to 100 percent over 90 ms.

options.label: Snap and pop
options.description: The highlight appears at once on the new row and the row pops slightly bigger. Snappy, like Destiny.
options.spec: Same demo stage, list and stepping as option A. MOTION: the highlight jumps to the new row in 0 ms; the new row scales 1.00 to 1.05 with easeOutBack c1 = 1.70158 over 160 ms (peak 1.055, which is 10 percent past the 1.05 target); the row that lost focus eases from 1.05 to 1.00 over 100 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1).

options.label: Fade swap and nudge
options.description: No travel: the old highlight fades out, the new one fades in, and the selected text slides right a little. Very calm.
options.spec: Same demo stage, list and stepping as option A. MOTION: old highlight opacity 1 to 0 over 90 ms; new highlight opacity 0 to 1 over 90 ms starting 40 ms later; the focused row's text translates 0 to +8px over 140 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1) (0 percent overshoot); the previous row's text returns 8 to 0 over 100 ms.

questions.pick_reason: A 4.6 percent spring is the 'little bounce' you asked for and it settles in under 200 ms, so a fast press never feels slow.

questions.title: The minimap frame
questions.context: The minimap is cut off by the screen edge today and the zone name prints over it and gets clipped. It needs a clean frame and a place for the name. Same map drawn with four frames.
questions.question: How should the minimap be framed?

options.label: Square, thin line
options.description: A square map with a thin border and the zone name below it. Matches the straight walls of the map.
options.spec: Backdrop: notes/shots/all4k/50-arcade-hud-live-4k.jpg cropped x806 y288 w2458 h1382 scaled to 1920x1080, full brightness. Palette: panel #0e1114, line #4a5257, text #f2efe6, muted #a9a79e, lime #e4ff2e, danger #ff5a3c, extract teal #47d8c6. Map content (all options): walls as light-grey lines #c9ccd0 on #0e1114, a lime arrow at the centre, three red dots (hostiles), a teal triangle (extraction) on the edge, three goal pins (lime star, teal diamond, red skull) and the zone name 'The long dock'. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: 300x300 at x1524 y54, fill rgba(14,17,20,.88), 1px #4a5257 border, radius 4px; north tag 'N' 18px top-left inside; zone name 24px muted right-aligned under the frame at y364 (never over the map).

options.label: Round radar
options.description: A circular radar with a view cone, like Halo. Looks sleek but crops the square map corners.
options.spec: Same backdrop and map content as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: circle 300px diameter at x1524 y54: fill rgba(14,17,20,.88), 3px #4a5257 ring plus a 1px inner ring at 10px inside; a lime wedge showing the view cone at 20 percent opacity; north tick; zone name 24px under it.

options.label: No frame, soft fade
options.description: The map fades into the world at its edges with no border. Subtle and stylish, a little harder to read.
options.spec: Same backdrop and map content as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: 340x340 at x1484 y40, map layer with a radial alpha mask (opaque to 70 percent of the radius, transparent at 100 percent); no border; markers drawn on top; zone name 24px muted under it with a 2px shadow.

options.label: Corner brackets
options.description: A dark map with four lime corner marks instead of a full border. Techy, keeps lime in the picture.
options.spec: Same backdrop and map content as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: 300x300 at x1524 y54, fill rgba(14,17,20,.8), no border; four lime corner brackets 28px long, 3px thick at the corners; 'N' in lime; zone name 24px muted under it.

questions.pick_reason: The map is full of straight walls, so a square frame crops nothing, and moving the zone name under it fixes the clipped label for good.

questions.title: The goals box
questions.context: You decided the box shows only 3 goals and every goal is also marked on the map. Today it is a long ragged list of contracts at tiny size. Same three goals in four looks.
questions.question: How should the three run goals look?

options.label: Plain list
options.description: A small box with three lines: a pin icon, the goal, and the SP reward. Done goals fade out.

options.label: Three mini cards

options.spec: Same backdrop, minimap ghost, pins and goals as option A. A done card flashes lime for 300 ms and slides out to the right.

options.label: Text on the world
options.description: No box at all: three lines with distances and little arrows pointing at each goal.
options.spec: Same backdrop, minimap ghost, pins and goals as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: no panel; right-aligned lines ending at x1824 starting y380 with a 40px pitch: 'Kill an elite   186 m   +400 SP' 28px white with a 2px black shadow and the SP part in lime; each line has a small 18px arrow pointing toward its pin; '3 pillagers' shows 1/3 as three small dots; done lines get a strike-through and fade.

options.label: A pill that opens

questions.pick_reason: Three short lines read from a TV in one glance, the matching pin colours tie each line to the map, and nothing needs a button to see.

questions.title: Alerts at the top centre
questions.context: Alerts like 'Hostiles closing in' or 'Extraction open' show up two or three times today (banner, toast and a small chip). One event should show once, in one place, big enough to read in a fight. Score and timer stay at the top centre.

options.label: One banner

One alert at a time; slides down 200 ms; shown 3 s. A small inset row (x640 y320) shows the same banner shape in teal for 'Extraction open' and in lime for 'Goal done'.

options.label: Big words only
options.description: Large text over the world with no box, a coloured underline and a quick pop-in.
options.spec: Same backdrop and top-centre score, timer and extraction chip as option A. STYLE FOR THIS OPTION: text only: 'Hostiles closing in' 64px white 800 centred at y230 with a 3px black shadow and a 6px danger underline bar 220px wide under it; subline 26px white at y300; pops in with scale 1.12 to 1.0 over 160 ms and stays 2.5 s. options.label: Banner plus red edge flash
options.description: The banner of option A plus a red glow around the screen edge for danger events only.
options.spec: Same backdrop, top-centre score, timer and extraction chip and banner (danger red) as option A. EXTRA FOR THIS OPTION: an inner red edge glow over the whole screen (inset 0 0 160px rgba(255,90,60,.35)) fading in over 150 ms and out over 600 ms, drawn at its peak; info and extraction banners (inset row) have no glow.

questions.pick_reason: One banner in one place says each thing once, and keeping lime, teal and red for goal, extraction and danger lets players read the type before the words.

questions.title: How much bounce
questions.context: You asked for livelier motion with a little bounce. 'A little' needs a number: how far a card or button overshoots before settling. Each option plays the same result card arriving, the score counting up and a button being pressed, with a different bounce.
questions.question: How much bounce should things have?

options.label: None
options.description: Everything eases to a stop. Crisp and calm, no bounce.
options.spec: Demo stage 640x400 on #0b0c0d: a result card 480x300 (fill #14171a, 1px #2e3337, 4px radius) shows 'Score' and '4,820 SP' 72px; loop 3 s: the card enters (translateY +48px to 0 and scale 0.92 to 1.00, opacity 0 to 1 over the first 40 percent), the score counts 0 to 4,820 over 900 ms starting 120 ms after the card, the score pops at the end, a lime 'Continue' button 200x56 fades in and is pressed (scale dip) at 1.6 s. CURVE FOR THIS OPTION: easeOutCubic f(t) = 1 - (1 - t)^3 for everything; overshoot 0 percent; card 220 ms; end pop none; button press scale 1 to 0.97 in 80 ms and back to 1 in 80 ms.

options.label: Light
options.description: A hair of overshoot on cards and a small pop on the score. Noticeable up close, never silly.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card, score and loop as option A. CURVE FOR THIS OPTION: easeOutBack f(t) = 1 + (c1 + 1)(t - 1)^3 + c1 (t - 1)^2 with c1 = 1.2: overshoot 5.3 percent of the travel (about 2.5 px on the 48px rise); card 240 ms; end score pop scale 1 to 1.06 to 1 over 160 ms; button press 1 to 0.96 and back to 1.00 over 140 ms with the same curve.

options.label: Lively
options.description: Clear overshoot on cards and a punchy score pop and button press. Feels like Fortnite and Halo 4.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card, score and loop as option A. CURVE FOR THIS OPTION: easeOutBack with c1 = 1.70158: overshoot 10.0 percent of the travel (about 4.8 px on the 48px rise); card 280 ms; end score pop scale 1 to 1.12 to 1 over 200 ms; button press 1 to 0.94 and back to 1.00 over 160 ms with the same curve.

options.label: Bouncy
options.description: Big overshoot and a wobble. Very playful, but it starts to look like a toy.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card, score and loop as option A. CURVE FOR THIS OPTION: easeOutBack with c1 = 2.8: overshoot 22.5 percent of the travel (about 10.8 px on the 48px rise); card 320 ms; end score pop scale 1 to 1.20 to 0.97 to 1 over 280 ms; button press 1 to 0.92 and back to 1.00 over 180 ms.

questions.pick_reason: A 10 percent overshoot is clearly livelier than the old 6 percent cap, still stays out of cartoon territory, and the score pop makes the big number land.

questions.title: Changing between tabs
questions.context: Switching a tab (Settings sections, stash filters) is the most repeated screen change after opening a menu. The content should arrive without making you wait or losing where you were. Each option plays a tab switch back and forth.
questions.question: How should the screen change when you switch tabs?

options.label: Fade and slide
options.description: The old rows fade and slide away while the new ones fade and slide in from the direction you pressed.
options.spec: Demo stage 560x360 on #0b0c0d: a card with a tab strip 'Raid', 'Audio', 'Controls' (28px, active white with a 4px lime underline) and four rows; the demo switches tab every 1.2 s (Raid, Audio, Controls, Audio, Raid; travelling right then left). MOTION: 200 ms total; outgoing rows opacity 1 to 0 over 100 ms while sliding 24px against the travel direction; incoming rows opacity 0 to 1 over 120 ms starting at 80 ms, sliding in from 24px on the travel side; easing cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); the underline follows x += (target - x) * (1 - exp(-dt / 0.05)) (95 percent in 150 ms), overshoot 0 percent.

options.label: Instant swap, springy underline
options.description: The rows swap at once with a very quick fade; only the underline moves, with a little spring.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and switching schedule as option A. MOTION: rows swap at 0 ms and fade in from opacity 0.6 to 1 over 60 ms, no slide; the underline is a spring with omega 28 rad/s and damping ratio 0.70: overshoot 4.6 percent of its travel, within 5 percent of the target by about 200 ms.

options.label: Rows rise in one by one
options.description: The old rows vanish fast and the new ones rise into place one after another. Lively without a bounce.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and switching schedule as option A. MOTION: outgoing rows disappear in 80 ms (opacity to 0, no movement); incoming rows rise from +12px: each row 160 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), starting 25 ms after the row above (with 4 rows the change is done at 235 ms, with 8 rows by 335 ms); the underline glides x += (target - x) * (1 - exp(-dt / 0.035)), overshoot 0 percent.

options.label: Carousel push
options.description: The pages sit side by side and slide together, so you feel which way you moved.
options.spec: Same demo stage, card and switching schedule as option A. MOTION: pages sit 480px apart; the outgoing page slides 480px against the travel and fades to 0; the incoming page slides in from 480px and fades in; both 280 ms with easeInOutCubic (t < 0.5: 4t^3, otherwise 1 - (-2t + 2)^3 / 2); the underline moves in sync; overshoot 0 percent.

questions.pick_reason: Staggered rows feel lively without any bounce on text you need to read, and the whole change is done in about a quarter of a second.
